headline: Revenue edges higher but margins compress on spin-off costs
summary_short: KBR's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 2% y/y to $1,984 million on Sustainable Technology Solutions growth, but operating income fell 11% y/y to $172 million on $31 million of Planned Spin-Off costs; net income attributable to KBR rose 32% to $96 million on a smaller drag from discontinued HomeSafe operations.
summary_long: Revenue grew 2% y/y to $1.98B as a 10% rise in Sustainable Technology Solutions (engineering and professional services) offset a 2% decline in Mission Technology Solutions (reduced European command contingent activity). Operating income fell 11% y/y to $172M, driven by $31M of Planned Spin-Off costs and STS licensing-mix headwinds, partly offset by MTS services-mix gains. Net income attributable to KBR rose 32% y/y to $96M because the prior-year quarter carried a $48M discontinued-operations loss tied to the HomeSafe wind-down, which is now largely resolved. Total backlog reached $17.8B, up from $16.9B at year-end. Cash fell to $312M on debt paydown and share repurchases; long-term debt declined slightly to $2.55B. No FY2026 guidance figures were reiterated or changed in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Increase driven by growth in engineering and professional services within Sustainable Technology Solutions (+10% y/y), partly offset by reduced contingent activity within the European command in Mission Technology Solutions.

Decline driven by $31M of Planned Spin-Off costs and lease right-of-use asset impairment charges, plus a less-favorable licensing mix within Sustainable Technology Solutions, partly offset by a favorable services mix in Mission Technology Solutions.

Prior-year quarter included a $48M net loss from discontinued operations tied to the HomeSafe joint-venture wind-down; that drag did not recur this quarter, more than offsetting the decline in operating income.
Gross profit was 'materially consistent,' moving in line with the revenue increase discussed above.

Cash declined after $161M of revolver paydowns, $42M of dividend payments, $25M of share repurchases and a $115M equity-method investment in the BRIS joint venture, partly offset by $141M of new revolver borrowings.

Management's discussion centers on the Mission Technology Solutions spin-off, targeted for completion January 4, 2027, and on defense-budget tailwinds (NDAA, U.K. and Australian defense investment); no numeric FY2026 guidance was restated in this filing.
